note: Append only log of prices read off a vendor pricing page. A new reading is a new entry with its own date. Nothing here is ever edited in place, because the point of the log is to show what was true when.

observations.billing: Monthly only. No annual option is offered anywhere on the pricing page, so an annual figure is twelve times the monthly one and carries no discount.
observations.model: Base price per tier plus a flat amount for every person on the team. The page asks how many cleaners and office managers are on the team and recalculates all three tiers. Verified linear across 0 to 12 people.

tiers.name: Pro Max
tiers.booking: Booking form carries your own branding

alsoRead: 14 day free trial on every tier
No setup fee is published, and contact import is offered free
Month to month, cancel any time, no contract
SMS charges are excluded from every tier price
observations.readBy: Read directly off the live pricing page, including driving the team size control through every value from 0 to 12 rather than taking the headline figures at face value.

observations.billing: Monthly or yearly. The yearly figure shown beside each plan is the annual total.
observations.model: Priced per route, not per person. The slider is labelled 'How many routes do you have?' and every plan states Unlimited Admin Users and Unlimited Mobile Devices, so headcount does not change the bill.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.booking: Customer Online Portal and Online Booking begin here, so this is the tier the site quotes
tiers.formula: 99 + 50 per additional route, verified exact from 1 to 12 routes

observations.readBy: Drove the route slider through every value from 1 to 12 and recorded all three tiers at each.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.note: Unlimited invoices, estimates, bills and bookkeeping records. Single user: adding users to the account is a Pro feature.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.note: Adds auto bank import, automated late payment reminders, unlimited receipt capture and the ability to add users.

observations.cardProcessing: 2.9% + $0.60 per credit card transaction, fixed fee waived on the first ten transactions a month on Pro.

observations.model: Three fixed tiers, no calculator and no slider. Base states Unlimited Users and Unlimited Bookings, so the flat quote holds at any crew size.

tiers.name: Base
tiers.note: Unlimited users, unlimited bookings, customer login portal, automated email reminders, booking form with Launch27 branding

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.note: Adds unbranded booking form, custom CSS, time tracking reports

observations.verdict: Flat quote confirmed correct. No user or booking cap a ten person crew would pass.

observations.model: Priced by number of locations cleaned, not headcount. Every plan includes unlimited users. All plans start at a minimum of fifteen locations, and the page bands locations at 1-15, 16-25, 26-30, 31-59 and 60+.
observations.notPublished: The page does not display what the higher location bands cost. Selecting a band did not reveal a figure without entering a gated flow, so bands above 15 locations are unread.
observations.verdict: The $30 quote is the entry price at the fifteen location minimum billed monthly, not a flat price. Headcount does not move it.

corrections.whatWasPublished: $39 a month at one, three and ten cleaners, on five guides and in the homepage docket, described as flat priced.
corrections.whatIsTrue: $39 is the Pro price with the team size calculator at its default of zero. The real Pro figures are $53 at one, $81 at three and $179 at ten, because the tier adds $14 a month for every person on the team.
corrections.cause: The calculator computes the prices in JavaScript and they are not in the page HTML, so a reading that did not drive the control saw only the zero position.
corrections.note: ZenMaid did not change its pricing. This is a correction to how the page was read, not a price movement.
corrections.noAugustEntry: This file was created on 2 October 2026 and has never held a 24 August observation, so there is no earlier entry to annotate. The August figures live only in the git history of the guides. The correction is recorded here rather than over anything.
